evidence.claim: GXO may map to outsourced retail/ecommerce fulfillment, reverse logistics, and warehouse automation nodes, but the provided evidence set does not yet verify retail/ecommerce revenue mix, contract quality, or automation economics.

InPost may map to parcel lockers and out-of-home ecommerce delivery networks, but the provided evidence set does not yet verify unit economics, utilization, country-level profitability, or competitive durability.

Shift4 may map to consumer transaction rails across hospitality, restaurants, venues, and ecommerce, but the provided evidence set does not yet verify vertical software attach, churn, net revenue economics, or acquisition quality.

Toast is a reference company for restaurant POS, payments, payroll, ordering, loyalty, and workflow software, but the provided evidence set does not yet verify current location growth, retention, fintech margins, or SMB churn.

PAR may be an underfollowed enterprise QSR infrastructure supplier with POS, loyalty, ordering, back-office, and payments exposure, but the provided evidence set does not yet verify ARR quality, customer concentration, acquisition integration, or FCF durability.

Olo may be a restaurant digital-order and delivery integration layer for enterprise chains, but the provided evidence set does not yet verify module attach, order volume durability, ARPU, churn, or marketplace dependency.

Lightspeed may map to SMB retail and restaurant commerce infrastructure, but the relationship is speculative until customer quality, churn, payments penetration, profitability, and sales efficiency are verified.

Commerce.com may contain product-feed and marketplace-integration infrastructure through Feedonomics, but the relationship is speculative because the provided evidence does not verify revenue materiality, retention, liquidity, debt, churn, or rebranding execution.

NCR Voyix may map to retail and restaurant POS, self-checkout, digital ordering, back-office, and related software/hardware systems, but the relationship is speculative due to post-separation complexity, leverage, and hardware legacy.

Graphic Packaging may map to consumer paperboard packaging, private-label packaging, food/beverage packaging, and foodservice packaging, but the provided evidence does not yet verify private-label exposure, pricing power, customer concentration, or sustainability-driven substitution.

memory_update.text: GXO maps to outsourced fulfillment, warehouse operations, reverse logistics, and automation-enabled contract logistics; keep as underfollowed hypothesis pending retail/ecommerce revenue mix, contract quality, and automation economics.

INPST.AS maps to parcel lockers and out-of-home ecommerce delivery networks; keep as underfollowed hypothesis pending country-level utilization, unit economics, capex intensity, and competitive-response checks.
FOUR maps to consumer transaction rails and vertical payments for hospitality, restaurants, venues, and ecommerce; verify software attach, churn, gateway/acquiring economics, and acquisition quality.
TOST should be treated as a reference benchmark for restaurant operating software and payments rather than an underfollowed alpha target.
PAR is a potentially underfollowed enterprise QSR software infrastructure candidate; verify ARR, enterprise wins, customer concentration, payments attach, acquisition integration, and FCF path.
OLO maps to restaurant digital ordering, delivery integration, and guest-data workflows; verify durable order volume, module attach, ARPU, retention, churn, and delivery marketplace dependency.

LSPD is a speculative-shadow SMB commerce software candidate; survival to later layers requires evidence of customer quality, lower churn, payment penetration, gross margin stability, and durable FCF.

CMRC is a micro-cap speculative-shadow candidate tied to product-feed management and marketplace integrations; requires urgent verification of Feedonomics materiality, liquidity, debt, retention, and churn.
NCRVOYIX maps to retail POS, self-checkout, restaurant software, and related hardware/software systems, but leverage, separation complexity, and hardware margin drag make it speculative.

GPK maps to consumer paperboard packaging and foodservice packaging; verify whether private-label, food/beverage volume, plastic substitution, and pricing power create a durable consumer infrastructure linkage.

The provided external evidence directly supports retail trading-partner networks and omnichannel supply-chain software, but not the specific economics of most tickers in this chunk; next layer must use primary filings and investor materials.
Need current market-cap, liquidity, valuation, debt, short interest, and analyst-coverage checks before promoting any candidate from relationship map to prioritized Layer 3 diligence.

Need node-level comparables: restaurant software should compare TOST, PAR, OLO, LSPD, NCRVOYIX; ecommerce fulfillment should compare GXO and INPST.AS against MANH/SPSC infrastructure benchmarks where appropriate.

summary: Mapped the candidate chunk into ticker-to-node relationships for the Consumer theme, with emphasis on underfollowed infrastructure rails rather than obvious consumer brands. Stronger relationships cluster around outsourced fulfillment, parcel lockers, restaurant commerce software, POS/payments rails, ecommerce catalog/feed integrations, and consumer packaging. Evidence quality remains preliminary because the provided external evidence directly supports retail EDI and omnichannel supply-chain software more than this specific chunk; most names therefore remain hypothesis-stage until filing-level revenue mix, customer concentration, recurring revenue, backlog, retention, and unit economics are verified.
